name: UK inflation & rates
summary: Bank of England raises Bank Rate to 4% on 5 Nov; warns inflation will near 5%
state: The Bank of England raised Bank Rate from 3.75% to 4% on 5 Nov, its first rise since 2023, reversing its easing cycle, and warned inflation will approach 5% (CNBC; Bank of England). UK CPI inflation was 3.5% in September, inside the 2.5–4.0% Watch band.
for_you: Variable and tracker mortgages, and new fixed deals, are likely to cost more; savings rates may rise.
rubric_hit: BoE reversing course and CPI 3.5% = Watch
basis_detail: ONS CPI and Bank of England decisions
basis_by: ONS CPI and Bank of England decisions

why: UK inflation and the Bank Rate set mortgage, savings and business borrowing costs for the whole country.
drivers: Energy prices, wages, services inflation, sterling, global rates.

rubric.alert: CPI > 4.0%, or an emergency BoE move.
rubric.watch: CPI 2.5–4.0%, or the BoE reversing course.
rubric.normal: CPI ≤ 2.5% and Bank of England moving gradually or on hold.
